newsitem.title: BELGIUM: UCB sees 1996 profits up significantly.
newsitem.headline: UCB sees 1996 profits up significantly.

text.p: Belgian chemicals and drug group UCB said on Thursday 1996 would show excellent profits, "significantly better than those of 1995."

In a statement on its research and investment programmes for 1997 it said the board approved a budget of research spending to the tune of 5.0 billion Belgian francs and an investment budget of 4.2 billion francs.
The research budget compared with 4.6 billion francs approved for 1996. "These programmes show the desire to continue efforts in research and development to strengthen expansion," UCB said.

On current performance UCB said that sales of its anti-allergy drug Zyrtec were progressing in every country. The U.S. launch continued to be successful. Interest in Nootropil, a treatment for cerebral dysfunction, was sustained in Europe and Asia.
The chemicals market remained favourable with activity since the summer "very satisfactory."
The trend in chemicals sales was good, particularly in the U.S., Asia and Latin America.
In films the development of speciality OPP films continued in applications such as coated films, self-adhesive labels and bank notes. In cellophane the level of activity remained firm.

In the first half of 1996 UCB had group net profit of 4,245 million francs, more than double the 1,984 million posted in the first half of 1995, on the back of one-off gains including a 1.7 billion franc gain from the sale of a UCB stake by a Luxembourg bank to a UCB shareholder via UCB and a gain from the sale of its packaging division to Amcor Group of Australia.
UCB had a full year 1995 operating profit of 5.14 billion francs and net profit of 3.26 billion francs.
